label: def:knot-operator-energy
title: Knot operator energy (LP-dual shadow price)
html:
Definition. Let H_n(R, q) be the Hecke algebra at substrate parameter q. For each Wedderburn block indexed by a partition \lambda \vdash k (k = 2, \ldots, k_{\max}(K, q), where k_{\max}(K, q) is the per-atom truncation determined by the interaction-strand requirement of K — see confinement level), the knot operator energy of \lambda at q is the absolute value of its LP-dual shadow price (prop:mass-coefficient-shadow-price):

  E(\lambda, q)
  \;:=\;
  \bigl| u_\lambda(q) \bigr|
  \;=\;
  \left|
    \frac{w_\lambda(q)}{d_\lambda(q)}
    \;-\;
    \frac{1}{[k]_q!}
  \right|,

where w_\lambda(q) = d_q(\lambda)^2 / [k]_q! is the Wedderburn weight, d_\lambda(q) = \dim_q V_\lambda is the quantum dimension, and 1/[k]_q! is \min_\lambda\, w_\lambda/d_\lambda, the minimum taken across partitions of k and attained by the trivial 1-dimensional (k) and (1^k) representations.

Note (2026-09-05). The subtrahend 1/[k]_q! was described here as "the LP-dual variable of the normalisation constraint". It is not: the net-constraint dual of the operator-selection LP is identically zero at every n and q, because the NF basis contains the identity and so the first Frobenius row is the objective vector. The quantity subtracted above is the weight minimum, which is what the displayed formula computes; the energy E(\lambda, q) is unchanged.

Values. The energy takes values in:

  • Archimedean realisation R = \mathbb{R}: E(\lambda, q) \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0} (totally ordered).
  • Non-archimedean \mathbb{Q}_p: E(\lambda, q) \in \{p^{-n} : n \in \mathbb{Z}\} \cup \{0\} (totally ordered).
  • Finite field \mathbb{F}_p: no archimedean absolute value exists. The energy filtration is undefined. Confinement falls back to ILP feasibility (see stable atom), which is base-ring-independent.
